name: Accountant and CPA
description: Accountants and auditors prepare, examine and attest to the financial records organisations run and are judged on — statements, tax, controls and the audits that make the numbers credible. ⚠ A median of $83,680 with 124,200 openings a year, one of the largest steady hiring markets on this site. ⚠⚠⚠ And the fact that should shape a Florida student's plan: Florida still requires 150 SEMESTER HOURS for a CPA licence while other states have moved, and bills to change it have passed the Florida Senate unanimously TWICE and died in the House both times. This page covers three related roles.
credentialNote: ⚠⚠ You can work as an accountant without a licence; you cannot sign an audit opinion without one. The BLS puts it plainly: any accountant who files a report with the Securities and Exchange Commission must be a licensed CPA. ⚠ Florida's requirements split into two numbers that people confuse constantly. To SIT the examination, s. 473.306(3)(a) requires 120 semester hours with a concentration in accounting and business courses prescribed by the Board of Accountancy. To be LICENSED, you need 150 semester hours — thirty more than a bachelor's degree — plus work experience and the four examination sections. ⚠⚠⚠ That thirty-hour gap is the central planning problem of this career, and it is why so many Florida students take a master's: it is usually the cheapest way to reach 150. Decide in your FIRST year, because a fifth year planned is far cheaper than a fifth year discovered. ⚠ Tax preparation needs no degree and no state licence — a federal PTIN and, to represent clients before the IRS, an Enrolled Agent credential or the CPA. Bookkeeping needs neither.
bodyHtml:
Three roles, and the gap between them is widening

Florida teaches these together and people move up between them, so this page covers the family.

RoleSOC2025 medianOutlook 2025–35Usual entry
Bookkeeping, accounting and auditing clerk43-3031$50,670⚠⚠ −6% declinesome college
Tax preparer13-2082$54,9205–6% growth⚠ 38% high school
Accountant or auditor13-2011$83,6805% growthbachelor's (69%)
and above: licensed CPA13-2011higher, and required to sign audits—⚠ 150 semester hours

⚠⚠⚠ The clerical tier is being automated away and the professional tier is not. The BLS is explicit: “software innovations have automated many of the tasks performed by bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks”, so “the same amount of work can be done with fewer employees” — 1,532,400 jobs falling by 85,600 over the decade. The same handbook notes clerks are expected to move into “a more analytical and advisory role”, which is a description of the skills that survive rather than a reassurance about the ones that do not.

⚠ It is still a real way in. “With appropriate experience and additional education, some bookkeeping, accounting, and auditing clerks may become accountants or auditors” — and in Florida, 40 public institutions teach the certificate against 13 that teach the degree, so for many students it is what is nearby. Take it as a start, with the degree already planned.

What the work actually is

O*NET, on accountants and auditors: prepare, examine, or analyze accounting records, financial statements, or other financial reports to assess accuracy, completeness, and conformance to reporting and procedural standards; compute taxes owed and prepare tax returns, ensuring compliance with payment, reporting, or other tax requirements; develop, implement, modify, and document recordkeeping and accounting systems, making use of current computer technology.

⚠ The demand is unusually steady. 124,200 openings a year against 1,595,200 jobs is a large, predictable hiring market that does not swing with a product cycle the way computing does — every organisation of any size needs this done, and much of it is required by law.

⚠⚠⚠ The 150-hour rule, and why Florida students must watch the legislature

To be licensed as a CPA in Florida you need 150 semester hours — thirty more than a bachelor's degree, for which nobody hands you an extra qualification unless you plan one. It is the single biggest cost and the single biggest deterrent in this career, and it is currently being dismantled across the country: the AICPA and NASBA approved alternatives to the 150-hour rule in May 2025, and state after state has legislated new pathways.

⚠⚠ Florida has tried twice and failed twice, both times in the same way.

BillWhat it would have doneWhat happened
CS/SB 160 (2025) Public Accountancyrevised the education and work-experience requirements for CPA licensurepassed the Senate 39–0 on 19 March 2025; ⚠ “Died in Messages” in the House, 16 June 2025
CS/SB 364 (2026) Public Accountancythe same reform, refiledpassed the Senate 35–0 on 29 January 2026; ⚠⚠ “Died in Messages” in the House, 13 March 2026

⚠⚠⚠ So as this page is written, Florida still requires 150 hours. The proposed alternatives — a master's plus one year of experience, or a bachelor's plus two years — are not law, and the Florida Institute of CPAs has said it intends to refile. Do not plan around a pathway that does not exist, and do not assume advice written for another state applies here.

⚠ What to actually do about it:

  • Decide in your first year whether you are going for the licence. Reaching 150 by design — a master's, a double major, or simply loading extra credits — is far cheaper than discovering the gap at graduation.
  • Remember you can sit at 120. Florida lets you take the examination on 120 hours, so you can pass it while completing the rest, which is what most successful candidates do.
  • ⚠⚠ Check the current rule before you commit money. This is the most likely thing on this page to change, and it will change by statute. The Board of Accountancy is the authority, not a review course's website.

✅ The best-travelling courses on this site

If you are starting at a Florida state college, this is the easiest transfer story of any career on this site. The lower-division business core is almost universally carried:

CourseCarriers
ECO 2023 Principles of Microeconomics✅ 39 of 39
ECO 2013 Principles of Macroeconomics38 — and it carries the (GE CORE) marker
ACG 2071 Managerial Accounting✅ 37 of 38 carriers of its prefix (97%)
ACG 2021 Financial Accounting32
BUL 2241 Business Law I25
TAX 2000 Personal Income Tax22

⚠⚠ But the upper division collapses, and that is where the real filter is. Intermediate Accounting — the course accounting students are actually weeded out by — runs as ACG 3101 (7 institutions), ACG 3103 (4) and ACG 3111 (5); auditing as ACG 4632 (7); cost as ACG 3341 (6). None above eight.

⚠ The good news is that this matters less here than elsewhere, because those courses live at the universities and the A.A. transfer protects the lower division you took at the college. The warning is different: intermediate accounting is a step change in difficulty, it arrives immediately after transfer, and students who coasted through the principles courses meet it badly.

Necessary skills

  • Precision sustained over long documents. The work is not hard in the way calculus is hard; it is hard in the way proofreading a thousand pages is hard.
  • Reading rules and applying them to facts. Accounting standards and tax code are law-like texts, and the job is the application.
  • Spreadsheet and systems fluency, moving toward data tools. The clerical tier vanished into software; the survivors are the people who run the software.
  • Scepticism. Auditing is a trained habit of not believing a figure because somebody respectable gave it to you.
  • Writing and explaining. Most of an accountant's value to a client is translating what the numbers mean into a decision they can take.
  • Ethical nerve. The pressure to sign something you are unsure of is the occupational hazard of the profession, and the licence is what you lose.

Advice

⚠⚠ Settle the 150-hour question in year one. It is the decision that determines your cost, your timeline and whether the CPA is available to you at all. And watch the legislature: two unanimous Senate votes suggest the reform will eventually pass, but it has not.

⚠ Take the lower division at a state college with confidence. ACG 2021, ACG 2071, ECO 2013 and ECO 2023 travel better than almost anything on this site — this is the rare path where the money-saving route carries almost no transfer risk.

⚠ Then take intermediate accounting seriously. It is the filter, it comes right after you transfer, and the principles courses do not predict it.

⚠ Do not stop at the bookkeeping certificate. It is a real job at 40 Florida institutions and it is projected to lose 85,600 positions nationally over the decade. Use it to get paid while you finish the degree, not instead of finishing it.

And get the internship. Public accounting recruits early, often in the penultimate year, and a busy-season internship is the usual route into the firms that pay for the fifth year.

cipCodes.note: Finance and financial management — 12 Florida public institutions and 2,968 graduates, the largest business code in the state after management. ⚠ A genuine adjacent feeder: many accounting roles are filled by finance graduates, and the two degrees share most of a first two years.
Business statistics and decision sciences — 8 Florida public institutions, 375 graduates. Included because the analytical half of accounting work is growing as the clerical half is automated away.

programs.note: The programme itself, at both tiers — 13 Florida public institutions for the degree and 40 for the bookkeeping certificate. ⚠ Read its degrees note before choosing: the certificate tier is projected to decline 6% while the degree tier grows, and the 150-hour rule shapes everything above the bachelor's.

⚠ Not a route to the licence, but increasingly part of the job — the clerical tier of accounting shrank because software absorbed it, and accounting information systems is where a growing share of the remaining work sits. ⚠⚠ An accounting degree plus real systems and data skills is a materially stronger position than either alone.

⚠ Not a route here. Named because the two are close neighbours at Florida state colleges — both rules-and-documents disciplines leading to credentialled work — and students weighing one often should weigh the other. Accounting pays more at the degree level; paralegal studies reaches a first job faster.

courses.reason: Financial Accounting — 32 institutions. The first real accounting course: the statements, the accounting equation, and whether this subject suits you. It is the gateway to every business major, not just this one.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Nine colleges instead run a two-course sequence, ACG2001 Financial Accounting I and ACG2011 Financial Accounting II, covering the same ground across two terms. ⚠⚠ Check which your college uses AND which your target university expects — this is the one lower-division place the packaging differs.

courses.reason: Managerial Accounting — 37 of the 38 institutions carrying the prefix, 97%: the best-travelling accounting course in Florida and one of the best-travelling on this site. Costing, budgeting and the internal numbers management actually decides on.
courses.variantNote: ✅ Take this at a state college with complete confidence. Almost nothing in Florida transfers more reliably.

courses.reason: Principles of Microeconomics — 39 of 39 institutions. The only course measured on this site that literally every Florida public institution carrying the prefix offers.
courses.variantNote: ✅ Universal. Required by every business degree in the state.

courses.reason: Principles of Macroeconomics — 38 institutions, and it carries the (GE CORE) marker, so it satisfies its general-education area at every Florida public college and university.
courses.variantNote: ✅ GE Core status means the area credit travels in transfer, not merely the credit hours — materially stronger than the ordinary transfer guarantee.

courses.reason: Business Law I — 25 institutions. Contracts, agency and the legal framework accounting operates inside, and a substantial part of the CPA examination's regulation section.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Some colleges run BUL2242 Business Law II (12 institutions) as a second term; universities more often teach BUL3130 The Legal Environment of Business (16) instead. Check which your degree requires.

courses.reason: Personal Income Tax — 22 institutions. Individual taxation from the preparer's side: the most immediately employable single course in this list, and the foundation of the tax-preparer role this page also covers.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ The upper-division equivalent is TAX4001 Individual Taxation (14 institutions), which is what an accounting bachelor's requires. They are not interchangeable for a degree requirement.

courses.reason: Computer Accounting Applications — 15 institutions. Practical accounting software, and the skill that separates someone who survives the automation of the clerical tier from someone displaced by it.

Intermediate Accounting I — 7 institutions. ⚠⚠ The real filter of an accounting degree: recognition, measurement and the standards in detail. It arrives immediately after transfer and the principles courses do not predict how hard it is.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ Carried as ACG3101 (7 institutions), ACG3103 (4) and ACG3111 for the second half (5) — the upper division of this prefix is fragmented where the lower division is near-universal. ⚠ Transfer on the syllabus here, and expect the receiving department to place you by content.

courses.reason: Cost Accounting I — 6 institutions. Product costing, variance analysis and the internal reporting that manufacturing and service firms manage by.

Auditing I — 7 institutions. Evidence, sampling, internal control and professional scepticism — the subject that distinguishes the licensed profession from bookkeeping, and a whole section of the CPA examination.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Only a licensed CPA may sign an audit opinion, so this course is where the reason for the licence becomes concrete.

courses.reason: Accounting Information Systems — 8 institutions. Controls, data flows and the systems the numbers live in. ⚠ The course most directly aimed at the part of this profession that is growing rather than being automated.
courses.variantNote: ⚠⚠ If your programme offers it as an elective, take it. The clerical tier of accounting was absorbed by software, and this is the course about running the software rather than being replaced by it.

courses.reason: Individual Taxation — 14 institutions, upper division. The degree-level tax course, and the foundation for the regulation section of the CPA examination.
Advanced Business Communication — 28 institutions. Most of an accountant's value to a client is explaining what the numbers mean, and this is the only course in the degree that teaches it explicitly.
Business Statistics and Analysis — 7 institutions. Sampling underpins auditing, and the analytical and advisory work the BLS says clerks must move toward rests on it.
courses.variantNote: ⚠ Carried under this number at only 7 institutions but required by most business bachelor's degrees under some number; STA2023 (39 institutions) is the usual lower-division substitute.

courses.reason: Elementary Statistics — 39 institutions. The lower-division statistics course most Florida business degrees accept, and the safest one to take at a state college.
English Composition I — 39 institutions. Audit findings, management letters and tax memoranda are written products, and in this profession the writing is part of the evidence.

sources.note: 1,595,200 jobs (2025), 5% growth 2025–35, +79,400, entry a bachelor's degree. ⚠ On the licence: any accountant who files a report with the SEC must be a licensed CPA, and all states require 150 semester hours — thirty more than a bachelor's.

sources.label: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook — Bookkeeping, Accounting and Auditing Clerks
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The shrinking tier: 1,532,400 jobs (2025), −6% decline 2025–35, −85,600, median $50,670, entry some college. The handbook names the cause — software has automated many of the tasks — and notes clerks are expected to move into a more analytical and advisory role. Some advance to accountant with experience and further education.

sources.label: O*NET — Tax Preparers (13-2082.00)
sources.note: The third role this page covers: 90,600 employed, growth 5–6% through 2034, 10,400 annual openings, median $54,920 (2025). ⚠ Education 38% high school, 24% postsecondary certificate, 24% bachelor's — the lowest entry bar in this family.

sources.label: Section 473.306, Florida Statutes — admission to the CPA examination
sources.note: ⚠ The number people confuse: s. 473.306(3)(a) requires 120 semester hours with a concentration in accounting and business courses prescribed by the Board of Accountancy to SIT the examination. Licensure requires 150.

sources.label: Florida Senate — CS/SB 160 (2025), Public Accountancy
sources.note: ⚠⚠ The first attempt to add alternative CPA pathways. Passed the Senate 39–0 on 19 March 2025; last action “Died in Messages” in the House, 16 June 2025. It did not become law.

sources.label: Florida Senate — CS/SB 364 (2026), Public Accountancy
sources.note: ⚠⚠⚠ The second attempt, revising education and work-experience requirements for CPA licensure. Passed the Senate 35–0 on 29 January 2026; last action “3/13/2026 House — Died in Messages.” It did not become law, so Florida still requires 150 hours.

sources.label: IPEDS Completions 2023 (C2023_A) — CIP 52.0301 and 52.0302
sources.note: The two tiers in numbers. Accounting degrees (52.0301): 13 Florida public institutions, 1,968 credentials — FAU 338, USF 316, FIU 285, UCF 276. ⚠ Bookkeeping and accounting technology (52.0302): 40 institutions, 1,872 credentials, overwhelmingly short certificates. Across both, 1,477 certificates against 1,419 bachelor's and 549 master's.
